content.title: I worked for the China Construction Engineering Bureau for six years, and last year I was promoted to project manager. Now I want to resign and change careers. Could you please give me some advice on what kind of work I can do?
content.body:
Hello!
Hello!
I am a student, as my experience and understanding are limited, what I say may not be comprehensive and reasonable. However, I will try to analyze your current issues as objectively as possible!
First, if you find that you cannot coordinate your work and life as a project manager, I support you in changing your job, but I do not recommend you to leave the construction industry.
Because you have spent six years on engineering projects, now jumping into other industries seems too costly. Your experience and network will be wasted. Not only that, as you yourself said, you don't know what industry to jump into. You just want to stop working on projects, and your future development goals are unclear. This will increase the probability of you jumping from one pit to another.
I hope you will carefully consider the current situation and make a rational decision, weighing the pros and cons before you decide.
Every line has its own challenges. I am a cost engineer, and I have also worked with my teacher on big data analysis, which is now very popular. Although I am young, I am a serious business analyst, but it looks glamorous on the outside, and the hardships are only known to me. Although the data industry can promote the development of traditional industries, ultimately, it is still service-oriented, and the initiative to create value does not lie with us. The first and second-hand data still lie in the hands of traditional industries and internet service industries. We are just doing the same job from different roles in a different model.
I think you don't want to do the current job anymore, you could try consulting services for real estate companies, which are still in the large industry background of civil engineering and construction. I'm not sure if you are the client or the contractor now. I think you are probably the contractor, you could check with the owner's side, give it a try! Or switch to a company as a project manager, I feel like you haven't had a lot of hardship until now, although I often argue that we shouldn't overly focus on sunk costs, I think for now, it's better not to give up without a clear goal.
I bet you've had entrepreneurial ideas too!
It's a coincidence that I have some knowledge about this policy. After observing and analyzing, my conclusion is that entrepreneurship is feasible, but it requires two resources: capital and connections. This is just the premise, not including whether your project has profitability and the opportunity for trial and error. It's quite challenging. By the way, the entrepreneurship I'm talking about is not about opening a small shop; it's about starting a business that is taxed as a company. Now, even opening a small shop or a restaurant is not easy. With so many restaurants out there, why would anyone buy from you, right?
In summary, carefully consider and make rational choices. It is suggested to leverage existing resources and consider becoming a project manager outside of the construction company, developing the business in the real estate or consulting services sector. Additionally, if you have a strong learning ability, you can use professional certificates as a stepping stone.
I hope it helps!

content.title: Is it better to pursue a master's and then a doctoral degree before working, or to work first and then pursue a master's and doctoral degree?
content.body:
Varies from person to person, a response biased towards science and engineering
If you like research and can handle the daily work of doing experiments, analyzing data, and reading literature, and you strive to publish papers every day, and you find new innovative points every time you read literature, then you should pursue a PhD (or a combined master's and doctoral program). If you are not very interested in research and just want to transition by getting a master's degree, then choosing a supervisor is an art. Supervisors who focus solely on research are not suitable for you, but those who work on industrialization and engineering are more suitable (those who focus on practical industry research). This way, you will have an easier time finding a job that matches your field after graduation, and you will be able to get up to speed quickly.
If your family's financial situation is difficult but you are passionate about scientific research, it is recommended to strive to get into a 985 university (with good majors, or 211 is also acceptable) because the subsidy standards (available on the official website) are higher than those of ordinary schools, ensuring basic living expenses. Additionally, with the availability of student loans, you can complete your studies without much financial burden from your family.
Working first can easily lead to getting stuck in a comfort zone, unless you have a lot of ideas and plans. If you can find a job you like and with a decent salary right after graduating from your undergraduate program, then just go for it.
In short, figure out what you really want as soon as possible and decide on your life direction. If you want to do research, you must pursue a Ph.D., and the sooner you get your degree, the better. If you are working for the money, then just go to work, after all, the opportunity cost is there.

content.title: Is it better for college students to take the postgraduate entrance exam or to start working directly?
content.body:
Now, most students who choose to pursue a postgraduate degree are no longer motivated by a simple passion for learning, but rather by a complex interplay of various personalities, values, and life attitudes. For college seniors, whether to pursue a postgraduate degree or enter the job market has become a real dilemma.
After the investigation, although the graduate school admission rate is as high as 3:1, if one fails to get in, they will have to choose to work or take the exam again next year. Working means wasting a year of time, and the employment difficulty will not be resolved; continuing to take the exam until admitted is an endless road. Moreover, pursuing a master's degree involves full-time study for another three years at school. Isn't this also a waste of time?
Expert Analysis:
1. Be pragmatic and avoid blindly following trends
Whether to pursue postgraduate studies or start working first is a matter of personal opinion. Generally, it depends on the overall situation. If the job market is favorable, it might be better to start working, but one must always remind oneself that even when working, one should continue to improve.
Everyone has their own dreams, their own pursuits, and their own goals. Different people have different experiences, backgrounds, and choices. Whether to pursue a postgraduate degree or enter the workforce, the decision should be based on one's own actual circumstances rather than blindly following the trend. If others choose to pursue a postgraduate degree, you should not automatically follow. Even if some people succeed in getting into graduate school through their own efforts, the employment prospects for their major may not be better a few years later. Such changes are difficult to accurately predict based solely on one's personal abilities. After graduating with a master's degree, your academic qualifications will be higher, but your social and practical experience will still be relatively limited compared to those who have already started working. In this sense, it may not be advantageous for employment.
2. Do not forget to improve yourself at work
Now, in many aspects, a bachelor's degree is no longer enough; at least a master's degree is required. For example, in the field of finance, the industry is developing rapidly, and financial products are constantly being innovated. Even with a master's degree, one may not fully understand them, so it's not right to think, "I have a master's degree, I know everything." Indeed, you might have graduated with a master's degree, but if you don't continue to learn, you still won't be able to keep up with the ever-evolving financial products. Another type of person to watch out for is those who, after graduating with a bachelor's degree and finding a well-paying job, then abandon their original intention to pursue a master's degree. Everyone will eventually hit a career bottleneck, and if you don't improve, you will fall behind in the competition. Therefore, don't let short-term benefits blind you to the need to improve yourself.
3. Work experience is more important than certificates
In a mature society, the evaluation of talent must be comprehensive, especially the evaluation of work experience. With the development of society, our talent standards have gradually shifted from blindly measuring by academic qualifications to evaluating by ability, placing increasing emphasis on work experience. Therefore, from a work perspective, two years of work experience are more important than two years of master's study. For many people, they pursue a master's degree because they cannot find a job, or because it does not meet their expectations.
4. Take responsibility for the future by adjusting your mindset
Shangyuan's warm reminder for postgraduate entrance examination candidates: Don't rush into blindly choosing between postgraduate studies or employment. First, find a direction that suits you, and then, based on industry conditions, development trends, and employment prospects, conduct a comprehensive analysis to decide whether to pursue postgraduate studies or employment. There is no clear consensus on whether postgraduate studies are beneficial for employment. However, one thing to note is that, regardless of whether you choose employment or postgraduate studies, you must have the right mindset and understand your own position. In a sense, postgraduate studies is an exam for adults. From the moment you make this decision, you must take responsibility for your future.
In short, there are roughly two types of people: one who sees pursuing a master's degree as a safe haven, unwilling to face the "hard knocks" of society; and the other who has no clear idea of what they truly need, lacking self-awareness and being vague, believing that they must obtain a master's degree. In fact, this is just deceiving oneself. Such master's students often end up wasting their time.
Finally, learning is a living knowledge that comes to life only when put into practice; otherwise, it is dead information. Whether for work or postgraduate studies, the expert in educational transition advises us: every great person starts with small things and grows through hardships, not by starting with great endeavors.

content.title: Should young people start a business?
content.body:
I think a lot of entrepreneurship is about timing and luck.
Maybe some people live a whole life without having this idea, but they still live very well. It all depends on whether you need to start a business, whether you want to start a business, and whether you have this need. If your current work and life are stable and you enjoy your current life, there is no need to choose to start a business.
I never thought about starting a business until I was 26. My life was comfortable, and my days were carefree. Why would I want to start a business that is so hard?
Until this year's New Year's Day when I broke up with my ex-boyfriend, I went through half a year of painful shadows. After that, I decided to start my own business (for various reasons, including personal ones). In any case, my initial investment was not large, and I was single, so I had no financial pressure. Therefore, I decided to go ahead and do it.
No matter whether I succeed or fail, I believe it will be an experience that accumulates experience in life. This experience will definitely help me grow quickly.

content.title: What exactly do you need to be prepared for entrepreneurship?
content.body:
Are you really ready for entrepreneurship?
There are ten reasons below that people should not start a business.
1、Become a boss,
2. To quickly become famous or wealthy,
3. Want to escape the boring work,
4. To solve a certain emotional issue,
5. Letting another person be satisfied,
6、Fad,
7. Don't miss the opportunity.
8. To add a little excitement to life,
9. Make life more meaningful
10, Change the world.
Reflect on yourself, have you fallen victim?
Entrepreneurship should be a strong impulse and passion to solve a social problem. You need to be prepared to work for the most autocratic and demanding boss in the world, especially when that boss is yourself. Can you accept the days when you are short of money and worrying about where to find the food for the next month? Are you ready to bear the most desperate and uncontrollable times of your life? If you can answer these questions with a confident yes, then you should definitely go into entrepreneurship.
The first step in entrepreneurship is to find the hidden needs of the user, as the main reason for entrepreneurial failure is often due to false needs. Have you validated your needs?
Why look for latent needs? Because there are too many people competing for explicit needs, and for ordinary people, there is no chance of success.

content.title: Which is more cost-effective, buying a house or renting an apartment?
content.body: This question depends on your needs. If your job is stable, you can choose to buy a house, and don't waste your housing fund. Of course, you need to consider the local housing prices, such as in Shenzhen. You can choose to rent a house, Shenzhen is a good place to live, and you can also read books while renting.
